'''Donald Wayne Sloan''' (born January 15, 1988) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M Aggies]]. Sloan played parts of five seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Atlanta Hawks]], [[New Orleans Hornets]], [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], [[Indiana Pacers]] and [[Brooklyn Nets]]. He played in the [[NBA D-League]] and [[Chinese Basketball Association]] in between NBA stints.

==High school career==
Sloan attended [[Seagoville]] High School in the [[Dallas]], Texas area. Over three seasons Sloan's team was 93–10 and Sloan led Seagoville to the regional championship game as a senior. Sloan received two-time all-state recognition.

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Sloan was listed as the No. 8 point guard and the No. 55 player in the nation in 2006.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Donald-Sloan-24956;_ylt=Apuq3xQX6jwCby1JSpwAM4lGPZB4 Donald Sloan Recruiting Profile]</ref>

Sloan was recruited by Kansas, Oklahoma, Marquette, SMU, and Georgia Tech. He signed with Texas A&M and Coach [[Billy Gillispie]] in November 2005.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aggieathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/110905aaa.html |title=Gillispie Signs Impressive Recruiting Class |publisher=ATM University |date=November 9, 2010 |access-date=March 9, 2010 }}{{dead link|date=September 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==College career==
Sloan played basketball for [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M University]] from 2006 to 2010. He was a part of a senior class that won 100 career games at the conclusion of the 2009–10 season, setting the school record for wins by a single class.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://media.www.thebatt.com/sports/aggie-men-clinch-bye-with-win-over-oklahoma-1.1258370 |title=Aggie men clinch bye with win over Oklahoma |publisher=ATM Battalion |date=March 7, 2010 |access-date=March 9, 2010 }}{{dead link|date=September 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> As a senior during the [[2009–10 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|2009–10 season]], Sloan led the Aggies in scoring with a 17.8 points per game average and was a first team All-[[Big 12 Conference]] selection.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=10410&ATCLID=204903228 |title=2010 Phillips 66 All-Big 12 Men's Basketball Awards Announced |publisher=Big 12 Sports |date=March 7, 2010 |access-date=March 9, 2010}}</ref>

===Freshman year===
Sloan appeared in all 34 games in 2006–07 as a true freshman, averaging 5.2 points, 1.9 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game.  Sloan earned ESPN player of the game honors with 15 points in a win at Oklahoma State.  Texas A&M finished the year with a 27–7 record and advanced to the [[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|Sweet Sixteen]].

===Sophomore year===
As a sophomore, Sloan started all 36 games as A&M  finished 25–11 after a second round robbery to UCLA in the NCAA tournament.  Sloan was third on the team in scoring at 9.5 points per game and he was second on the team with 123 assists.

===Junior year===
Sloan played in all 34 games as the Aggies finished 24–10 following a second round loss to Connecticut in the NCAA tournament.  Sloan averaged 11.8 points and 3.6 rebounds per game and led the team with 108 assists.

===Senior year===
Sloan, considered by his teammates to be the team's leader,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://ncaabasketball.fanhouse.com/2010/02/15/sloan-is-aandms-rock-as-aggies-roll/ |title=Sloan Is A&M's Rock as Aggies Roll |publisher=NCAA Basketball Fanhouse |date=February 15, 2010 |access-date=March 10, 2010 |archive-date=February 17, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100217071101/http://ncaabasketball.fanhouse.com/2010/02/15/sloan-is-aandms-rock-as-aggies-roll/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/sports/college/texas/6888551.html |title=The word on Sloan is he's good: A&M players impressed with senior's literary talent, leadership |work=Houston Chronicle |date=February 27, 2010 |access-date=March 10, 2010}}</ref> was the leading scorer on a Texas A&M team that finished the regular season with a 22–8 record overall and an 11-5 conference mark, tying the team for second place in the Big 12 Conference.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/joe_lemire/02/17/texas.am/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100221013621/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/joe_lemire/02/17/texas.am/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 21, 2010 |title=Donald Sloan leading Texas A&M Aggies toward NCAA tournament bid |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=February 17, 2010 |access-date=March 10, 2010}}</ref>  Sloan scored a career high 29 points in an 84–81 loss to New Mexico on December 12.  He was third in the Big 12 in scoring.<ref>Zwerneman, Brent. [http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/sports/college/texas/6888551.html Well-rounded Sloan emerges as leader for A&M], ''Houston Chronicle'', February 27, 2010.</ref> Sloan was named to the Big 12's first team all conference by Big 12 coaches, Dallas Morning News,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/spt/colleges/topstories/stories/030910dnspodmnbig12men.3e7efeb.html |title=OSU's Anderson earns DMN's Big 12 men's player of the year |publisher=Dallas Morning News |date=March 8, 2010 |access-date=March 9, 2010}}</ref> Columbia Daily Tribune, and [[Fort Worth Star Telegram]]. Sloan also received second team all Big 12 Conference honors from the [[Associated Press]] and Austin American-Statesman.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.statesman.com/sports/american-statesmans-all-big-12-mens-basketball-team-333031.html |title=American-Statesman's All-Big 12 men's basketball team |publisher=Austin American-Statesman |date=March 8, 2010 |access-date=March 9, 2010 |archive-date=June 7, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110607055426/http://www.statesman.com/sports/american-statesmans-all-big-12-mens-basketball-team-333031.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He received national player of the week honors for the week of February 9 by CollegeHoops.net and was a strong contender for the 2009–2010 Big 12 Conference Player of the Year Award.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/colleges/post/_/id/4666568/add-ams-sloan-to-big-12-mvp-race |title=Add A&M's Sloan to Big 12 MVP race |publisher=ESPN Dallas: By Jeff Caplan |date=February 4, 2010 |access-date=March 10, 2010}}</ref> Sloan honored teammate and close friend Derrick Roland, whose season was ended by a broken tibia and fibula, by shaving Roland's #3 into his hair for much of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/aggies/Focused_Aggies_roll_honor_injured_Roland.html |title=Focused Aggies roll, honor injured Roland |publisher=San Antonio Express News |date=January 3, 2010 |access-date=March 9, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100106061358/http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/aggies/Focused_Aggies_roll_honor_injured_Roland.html |archive-date=January 6, 2010 }}</ref>

Following the conference tournament, Sloan was named to the all-tournament team.<ref>[http://www.kansascity.com/2010/03/13/1811107/big-12-all-tournament-team.html Big 12 all-tournament team], KansasCity.com, March 14, 2010.</ref> He finished the 2010 NCAA tournament ranked seventh in Aggie history in career scoring with 1,522 points and eighth in assists with 370.

==Professional career==

===Reno Bighorns (2010–2011)===
After going undrafted in the [[2010 NBA draft]], Sloan joined the [[Sacramento Kings]] for the 2010 [[NBA Summer League]].<ref>[http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2010/6/28/1540775/nba-summer-league-rosters-vegas NBA Summer League Rosters - Vegas]</ref> He later signed a one-year, non-guaranteed contract with the Kings.<ref>[http://www.sactownroyalty.com/2010/7/9/1561880/kings-sign-donald-sloan-to-1-year Kings Sign Donald Sloan to 1-Year Deal]</ref> However, he was later waived by the Kings on October 4, 2010.<ref>[http://www.sactownroyalty.com/2010/10/4/1730545/j-r-giddens-donald-sloan-waived-by-kings J.R. Giddens, Donald Sloan Waived by Kings]</ref> On October 30, 2010, he was acquired by the [[Reno Bighorns]] of the [[NBA D-League]] as an affiliate player.

===Barangay Ginebra Kings (2011)===
In July 2011, he signed with the [[Barangay Ginebra Kings]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] for the 2011 Governors' Cup.<ref>[http://www.ballerspinas.com/2011/07/new-import-of-ginebra-gin-kings-is.html The New Import of Ginebra Gin Kings is Donald Sloan He will Replace Curtis Stinson for the Rest of the Governors' Cup 2011]</ref>

===Erie BayHawks (2011)===
On November 2, 2011, he was reacquired by the Reno Bighorns. Two days later, he was traded to the Erie BayHawks.

===Atlanta Hawks (2011–2012)===
On December 9, 2011, Sloan signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. On January 27, 2012, he was waived by the Hawks.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/Sloan_Waivers_PR.html HAWKS REQUEST WAIVERS ON DONALD SLOAN]</ref>

===New Orleans Hornets (2012)===
On February 8, 2012, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[New Orleans Hornets]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_sign_donald_sloan_2012_02_08.html Hornets Sign Donald Sloan]</ref> On February 18, 2012, he was not offered a second 10-day contract after his first 10-day contract expired.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.hornets247.com/blog/2012/02/29/donald-sloan-wont-be-extended-another-10-day-contract/ |title=Donald Sloan Won't be Extended Another 10-Day Contract |access-date=March 16, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120305040010/http://www.hornets247.com/blog/2012/02/29/donald-sloan-wont-be-extended-another-10-day-contract/ |archive-date=March 5, 2012 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

===Return to Erie (2012)===
On March 5, 2012, he returned to the Erie BayHawks.

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2012)===
On March 16, 2012, he signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] .<ref>[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/sloan_120316 Cavaliers Sign Donald Sloan]</ref>

In July 2012, he joined the Cavaliers for the 2012 NBA Summer League. On December 25, 2012, Sloan was waived by the Cavaliers.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/livingston-sloan-121225 Cavaliers Claim Shaun Livingston Off Waivers, Waive Donald Sloan]</ref> On the Aussie Hoopla podcast Sloan discussed how he was brought into back-up rookie Kyrie Irving, however Irving become injured as soon as Sloan was signed and then after Irving became healthy the Cavs waived Sloan on Christmas Day.<ref>{{cite web|last=Boyce|first=Dan|url=http://www.aussiehoopla.com/donald-sloan-adelaide-36ers-indiana-pacers-cleveland-cavaliers/|title=Donald Sloan (Adelaide 36ers) on backing up Kyrie Irving, funny Lance Stephenson stories & more|work=aussiehoopla.com|date=15 September 2020|access-date=20 October 2020}}</ref>

===Return to New Orleans and Sioux Falls (2013)===
On January 3, 2013, he was acquired by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/siouxfalls/three_team_trade_130103.html |title=Skyforce Acquires Two Former NBA Players in Three-Team Trade |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=January 4, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714201527/http://www.nba.com/dleague/siouxfalls/three_team_trade_130103.html |archive-date=July 14, 2014 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> On January 7, 2013, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[New Orleans Hornets]] after just two games with the Skyforce.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-sign-donald-sloan-10-day-contract HORNETS SIGN DONALD SLOAN TO 10-DAY CONTRACT]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/sioux_falls_donald_sloan_sign_2013_01_07.html |title=Sioux Falls' Donald Sloan Signs with the New Orleans Hornets |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=January 8, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130110184321/http://www.nba.com/dleague/sioux_falls_donald_sloan_sign_2013_01_07.html |archive-date=January 10, 2013 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> After the contract expired, he returned to the Skyforce.

===Guangdong Southern Tigers (2013)===
In February 2013, Sloan was released by the Skyforce in order to join the [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>[http://espn991.com/skyforce-lose-point-guard-donald-sloan-to-china/ Skyforce Lose Point Guard Donald Sloan to China]</ref><ref>[http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2013/02/donald-sloan-to-sign-in-china.html Donald Sloan Signs In China]</ref>

===Indiana Pacers (2013–2015)===
[[File:John Wall, Donald Sloan (15723872952).jpg|thumb|right|Sloan defended by [[John Wall]] of the [[Washington Wizards]] during a 2014 game]]
On July 3, 2013, he signed a two-year deal with the [[Indiana Pacers]] and joined them for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/solomon-hill-donald-sloan-signed Solomon Hill, Donald Sloan Signed]</ref> In July 2014, he re-joined the Pacers for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Rookie/Free Agent Camp Update|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/rookie/free-agent-camp-update|access-date=July 8, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=July 3, 2014}}</ref> On November 5, 2014, he scored a career-high 31 points in the Pacers' 96–94 overtime loss to the Washington Wizards.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141105/INDWAS/gameinfo.html |title=Wizards win 4th in row, top Pacers 96-94 in OT |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=November 6, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150312195255/http://www.nba.com/games/20141105/INDWAS/gameinfo.html |archive-date=March 12, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2015–2016)===
On August 10, 2015, Sloan signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/brooklyn-nets-sign-donald-sloan|title=BROOKLYN NETS SIGN DONALD SLOAN|work=NBA.com|date=August 10, 2015|access-date=August 10, 2015}}</ref> On January 15, 2016, he recorded a near triple-double with 15 points, 9 rebounds and 9 assists in a loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160115/PORBKN/gameinfo.html |title=Lillard has 33 points, Blazers beat Nets, win 3rd straight |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=January 16, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160118191422/http://www.nba.com/games/20160115/PORBKN/gameinfo.html |archive-date=January 18, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Return to Guangdong (2016–2017)===
On July 20, 2016, Sloan signed with the Guangdong Southern Tigers for the 2016–17 season, returning to the club for a second stint.<ref>[https://twitter.com/ImpactSportsInc/status/755760095364014084 Client @DSloan15 has signed a contract with the...]</ref> The Guangdong Southern Tigers advanced to the [[2017 CBA Playoffs#Finals|2017 CBA Finals]], but lost to the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]] in a 4–0 sweep.

=== Texas Legends (2017–2018) ===
Sloan signed with the [[Washington Wizards]] under a training camp deal. He was waived on October 14 as one of the team's final preseason roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Wizards waive Donald Sloan|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-waive-donald-sloan|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 14, 2017|date=October 14, 2017}}</ref> He then joined the [[Texas Legends]] of the NBA G League. On January 22, 2018, Sloan was named the [[NBA G League]] Player of the Week after averaging 29.0 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 9.0 assists in three games.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://gleague.nba.com/news/donald-sloan-named-nba-g-league-player-week/|title=Donald Sloan Named NBA G League Player Of The Week|date=January 22, 2018|work=[[National Basketball Association]]|access-date=January 29, 2018}}</ref>

===Third stint with Guangdong (2018)===
On February 21, 2018, [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] announced the signing of Sloan for a third stint with the team.<ref>{{cite news|title=再换小外援!昔日夺冠功臣加盟广东 斯隆第三次来粤|url=http://sports.163.com/18/0221/15/DB6872DV0005877V.html|access-date=February 21, 2018|publisher=网易体育}}</ref>

Sloan signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]] to a training camp contract but was waived on October 13, 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=We have waived Xavier Silas and Donald Sloan.|url=https://twitter.com/nuggets/status/1050962172149297152|access-date=October 16, 2018 |work=twitter.com|date=October 13, 2018}}</ref>

===Telekom Baskets Bonn (2020)===
On February 26, 2020, Sloan signed with [[Telekom Baskets Bonn]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/donald-sloan-joins-telekom-baskets-bonn/|title=Donald Sloan joins Telekom Baskets Bonn|date=February 26, 2020|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=February 26, 2020|last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }}</ref> He played in three games and averaged 11.7 points per game until the season was postponed due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Uluc |first1=Olgun |title=NBL: Adelaide 36ers sign former Pacers guard Donald Sloan |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nbl/story/_/id/29641804/nbl-adelaide-36ers-sign-former-pacers-guard-donald-sloan |website=ESPN |access-date=November 3, 2020 |date=August 12, 2020}}</ref>

===Adelaide 36ers (2020–2021)===
On August 20, 2020, Sloan signed with the [[Adelaide 36ers]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL).<ref>{{cite web |title=Adelaide 36ers Sign US Import Donald Sloan |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/adelaide-36ers-sign-us-import-donald-sloan |website=NBL.com.au |access-date=August 20, 2020 |date=August 20, 2020}}</ref> He scored three points in his NBL debut against [[Melbourne United]] on January 15, 2021.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ward |first1=Roy |title=United storm home in NBL opener |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/united-storm-home-in-nbl-opener-20210115-p56ubv.html |website=The Sydney Morning Herald |access-date=February 7, 2021 |date=January 15, 2021}}</ref> Sloan was moved from the starting line-up in favor of [[Josh Giddey]] and scored a season-high 20 points in his first game off the bench on January 22, 2021, against the [[New Zealand Breakers]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Humphries stands tall as 36ers beat Breakers in OT |url=https://www.adelaide36ers.com/news/humphries-stands-tall-as-36ers-beat-breakers-in-ot |website=Adelaide 36ers |access-date=February 7, 2021 |date=January 22, 2021}}</ref> On February 7, 2021, he was granted a release by the 36ers to pursue other international opportunities.<ref>{{cite web |title=Donald Sloan Granted Release by Adelaide 36ers |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/donald-sloan-granted-release-by-adelaide-36ers |website=NBL.com.au |access-date=February 7, 2021 |date=February 7, 2021}}</ref>
